sentence: The new law will ___ every driver in the country.
explanation: 'Affect' is the verb meaning to have an influence on; 'effect' is normally a noun meaning a result.

sentence: The medicine had an immediate ___ on her pain.
hint: a noun is needed after 'an immediate'
explanation: 'Effect' is the noun meaning result; the fixed phrase is 'have an effect on something'.

sentence: The new regulations came into ___ last month.
explanation: 'Come into effect' means to start being used; 'affect' is a verb and cannot follow 'into'.

sentence: Can you ___ me on which course to choose?
explanation: 'Advise' is the verb (to give advice); 'advice' is the uncountable noun and 'advices' does not exist.

sentence: She gave me some useful ___ about buying a house.
hint: a noun is needed after 'some useful'
explanation: 'Advice' is the uncountable noun; 'advise' is the verb. 'Advices' is not standard English.

sentence: We ___ all major credit cards at the box office.
explanation: 'Accept' means to take or agree to something offered; 'except' means not including.

sentence: The museum is open daily ___ Mondays.
explanation: 'Except' means not including; 'accept' is a verb meaning to take willingly.

sentence: Be careful not to ___ your keys on the bus.
hint: a verb is needed; meaning: no longer have
explanation: 'Lose' is the verb (opposite of find); 'loose' is an adjective meaning not tight.

sentence: This tooth is ___ and will probably fall out soon.
explanation: 'Loose' is an adjective meaning not firmly fixed; 'lose' is the verb meaning to no longer have.

sentence: Please be ___ — the baby is sleeping.
explanation: 'Quiet' means making little or no noise; 'quite' is an adverb meaning fairly or completely.

sentence: The film was ___ good, but not brilliant.
hint: an adverb of degree is needed before 'good'
explanation: 'Quite' means fairly or rather; 'quiet' is an adjective meaning without noise.

sentence: A car remained ___ at the traffic lights for ages.
explanation: 'Stationary' means not moving; 'stationery' means pens, paper and other writing materials.

sentence: Pens, envelopes and paper are sold in the ___ department.
explanation: 'Stationery' means writing materials; 'stationary' is an adjective meaning not moving.

sentence: The wine ___ the meal perfectly.
explanation: 'Complement' means to combine well with or complete something; 'compliment' means to praise.

sentence: He ___ her on her excellent presentation.
explanation: 'Compliment somebody on something' means to praise; 'complement' means to go well with.

sentence: The ___ reason for the delay was the weather.
hint: adjective meaning main or most important
explanation: 'Principal' as an adjective means main or most important; 'principle' is a noun meaning a basic rule or belief.

sentence: She refuses to lie on ___.
hint: noun meaning a moral rule; fixed phrase 'on principle'
explanation: 'On principle' means because of a moral belief; 'principal' means main or the head of a school.

sentence: After dinner we had chocolate cake for ___.
hint: the sweet course of a meal (double 's' like 'sweet stuff')
explanation: 'Dessert' is the sweet course at the end of a meal; 'desert' is a dry, sandy region.

sentence: The Sahara is the largest hot ___ in the world.
explanation: 'Desert' is a dry region with little rain; 'dessert' is the sweet course of a meal.

sentence: Thousands of people were forced to ___ their homes.
hint: a verb is needed after 'to'; meaning: abandon
explanation: 'Desert' is also a verb meaning to abandon; 'dessert' is only the sweet course of a meal.

sentence: It costs more ___ I expected.
explanation: 'Than' is used in comparisons; 'then' refers to time or consequence.

sentence: We had lunch, and ___ we went for a walk.
explanation: 'Then' means next or after that; 'than' is used in comparisons.

sentence: The children left ___ toys all over the floor.
explanation: 'Their' shows possession; 'there' is a place; 'they're' means 'they are'; 'theirs' is a possessive pronoun standing alone.

sentence: Look at that bird up ___ in the tree.
explanation: 'There' refers to a place; 'their' shows possession; 'they're' means 'they are'.

sentence: The company has changed ___ logo twice.
explanation: 'Its' is the possessive form of 'it'; 'it's' means 'it is' or 'it has'. 'Its'' does not exist.

sentence: ___ been raining all week.
explanation: 'It's' is short for 'it is' or 'it has'; here it means 'it has been raining'. The possessive is 'its'.

sentence: ___ coming to the party tonight?
explanation: 'Who's' is short for 'who is'; 'whose' asks about possession.

sentence: Do you know ___ bag this is?
explanation: 'Whose' asks about possession; 'who's' means 'who is'.

sentence: Don't forget to bring ___ umbrella.
explanation: 'Your' shows possession; 'you're' means 'you are'; 'yours' is a possessive pronoun standing alone.

sentence: ___ going to love this film.
explanation: 'You're' is short for 'you are'; 'your' shows possession.

sentence: I'm exhausted — I need to ___ down and rest.
hint: to recline — no object; forms: lie, lay, lain
explanation: 'Lie' (lie, lay, lain) means to recline and takes no object; 'lay' (lay, laid, laid) means to put something down and takes an object.

sentence: She ___ the documents on the desk and left.
hint: past of the verb meaning 'put down' (takes an object)
explanation: 'Laid' is the past of 'lay' (put something down), which takes an object: she laid the documents.

sentence: He ___ on the sofa all afternoon yesterday.
explanation: 'Lay' is the past of 'lie' (recline): he lay on the sofa. 'Laid' would need an object.

sentence: Sales have ___ sharply since January.
hint: past participle after 'have'; the verb takes no object
explanation: 'Rise' (rise, rose, risen) takes no object: sales have risen. 'Raise' takes an object: they raised prices.

sentence: The government plans to ___ taxes next year.
hint: the verb takes an object: taxes
explanation: 'Raise' means to lift or increase something (takes an object); 'rise' means to go up (no object).

sentence: Smoke could be seen ___ from the factory chimneys.
hint: the smoke goes up by itself — no object
explanation: 'Rise' (no object) describes the smoke going up; 'raise' would need an object (raise something).

sentence: Could I ___ your pen for a moment?
hint: meaning: take and return later (from someone's point of view)
explanation: 'Borrow' means to take something temporarily; 'lend' means to give something temporarily to someone else.

sentence: The bank agreed to ___ him the money.
hint: meaning: give temporarily (from the giver's point of view)
explanation: 'Lend' means to give something to someone temporarily; the bank lends money. A base verb is needed after 'to'.

sentence: She ___ me a fascinating story about her childhood.
hint: telling a story to a person: ___ + person + story
explanation: 'Tell' takes a person as object: tell somebody a story. 'Say' does not take the listener directly.

sentence: He ___ that he would be late.
hint: '___ that ...' without a listener as object
explanation: 'Say' is used with reported content ('say that ...') without a person object; 'tell' needs one (tell me that ...).

sentence: Can you ___ the difference between these two words?
explanation: 'Tell the difference' is a fixed expression meaning to see or know how things differ.

sentence: Our team ___ the match 3-0.
hint: you ___ a match, but ___ the other team
explanation: 'Win' takes the game or prize as object (win a match); 'beat/defeat' take the opponent as object.

sentence: They managed to ___ the champions in the final.
explanation: 'Beat' takes the opponent as object (beat the champions); 'win' takes the game or prize.

sentence: Please ___ me to post this letter.
hint: make somebody not forget: ___ somebody to do something
explanation: 'Remind somebody to do something' means to make someone remember; 'remember' is something you do yourself.

sentence: I can still ___ the day we first met.
hint: to keep in your memory yourself
explanation: 'Remember' means to keep something in your memory; 'remind' means to make someone else remember.

sentence: This smell ___ me of my childhood.
explanation: 'Remind somebody of something' means to make someone think of something; 'remember' is not followed by an object + of.

sentence: We spent the evening ___ television.
hint: the standard verb with television and sport
explanation: 'Watch television' is the fixed collocation; 'look' needs 'at', and 'see television' is not used.

sentence: Did you ___ the new exhibition at the museum?
hint: to visit and experience something like an exhibition or film
explanation: 'See an exhibition' means to visit and view it; 'watch' is used for moving images and events.

sentence: ___ at this old photo — isn't it amazing?
explanation: 'Look at' means to direct your eyes towards something; the other verbs cannot be followed by 'at' here.

sentence: I couldn't ___ what he was saying because of the noise.
explanation: 'Hear' means to receive sound; 'listen' means to pay attention deliberately and needs 'to'.

sentence: We sat ___ to the sound of the waves.
explanation: 'Listen to' means to pay attention to sound deliberately; after 'sat' the -ing form is needed.

sentence: The train ___ was delayed by two hours.
hint: the act of travelling from A to B, especially by land or rail
explanation: 'Journey' is an act of travelling from one place to another; 'voyage' is by sea; 'travel' is uncountable.

sentence: We went on a school ___ to the coast.
hint: a short outing with a return, often for pleasure or a purpose
explanation: 'Trip' is a short journey with a return ('a school trip'); 'voyage' is a long journey by sea.

sentence: The Titanic sank on her maiden ___.
explanation: 'Voyage' is a long journey by ship or spacecraft; 'maiden voyage' is a ship's first journey.

sentence: ___ broadens the mind.
hint: the uncountable activity of travelling in general
explanation: 'Travel' is uncountable when it means travelling in general; the other options are countable nouns.

sentence: Air ___ has become much cheaper in the last twenty years.
hint: uncountable noun for travelling in general
explanation: 'Air travel' is the fixed expression for travelling by plane; 'travel' is uncountable here.

sentence: She has had a brilliant ___ in politics.
hint: the whole course of a person's professional life
explanation: 'Career' is the progress through a working life, especially in one profession; 'job' is one position.

sentence: I start my new ___ at the hospital on Monday.
hint: a single, countable position of employment
explanation: 'Job' is countable — one particular position; 'work' is uncountable and cannot follow 'a new'.

sentence: After graduating he struggled to find ___ for several months.
explanation: 'Work' is uncountable, so it fits after 'find' with no article; 'job' would need 'a job'.

sentence: Please state your ___ on the application form.
hint: the formal word for your type of work, used on forms
explanation: 'Occupation' is the formal word for a person's job or profession, typically used on official forms.

sentence: Her annual ___ is reviewed every April.
hint: fixed regular pay for professional work, usually monthly
explanation: 'Salary' is fixed regular pay for professional or office work, usually paid monthly; 'wages' are usually weekly.

sentence: Factory workers are paid ___ at the end of each week.
hint: pay for manual work, usually weekly
explanation: 'Wages' are paid weekly, often in cash, for manual or unskilled work; salaries are monthly.

sentence: The lawyer's ___ is 200 pounds an hour.
hint: money paid to a professional for one service
explanation: 'Fee' is the amount charged by a professional such as a lawyer or doctor for a particular service.

sentence: Tax is calculated on your total annual ___.
hint: all the money you receive from every source
explanation: 'Income' is all the money you receive from work, investments, rent and so on during a period.

sentence: The two leaders signed a ___ peace agreement.
hint: important enough to be remembered in history
explanation: 'Historic' means important or famous in history; 'historical' just means connected with the past or the study of history.

sentence: The book gives a detailed ___ account of the period.
hint: connected with the study of the past
explanation: 'Historical' means relating to history or the past; 'historic' means important in history.

sentence: The country is facing a serious ___ crisis.
hint: connected with money, trade and industry
explanation: 'Economic' means connected with the economy; 'economical' means saving money.

sentence: This small car is very ___ to run.
explanation: 'Economical' means costing little or saving money; 'economic' relates to trade, industry or the economy.

sentence: It would be ___ to take an umbrella — the sky is black.
explanation: 'Sensible' means showing good judgement; 'sensitive' means easily affected by things or feelings.

sentence: He is very ___ to criticism and takes it personally.
hint: easily affected or hurt; pattern: ___ to
explanation: 'Sensitive to something' means easily affected or upset by it; 'sensible' means showing good judgement.

sentence: The ___ cost was much higher than the estimate.
explanation: 'Actual' means real or existing in fact; 'current' means belonging to the present time.

sentence: The ___ issue of the magazine has an interview with the president.
explanation: 'Current' means happening or existing now; 'actual' means real as opposed to possible or estimated.

sentence: I was so ___ when I forgot her name in front of everyone.
hint: how you feel in an awkward social situation
explanation: 'Embarrassed' describes short-term discomfort in a social situation; 'ashamed' implies guilt about wrongdoing.

sentence: He should be ___ of himself for lying to his friends.
hint: feeling guilt about something you did; pattern: ___ of
explanation: 'Ashamed of' means feeling guilt or shame about behaviour; 'embarrassed' is only social discomfort.

sentence: The ___ of repairing the roof was higher than we expected.
hint: the amount of money needed to do something
explanation: 'The cost of doing something' is the money needed to do it; 'price' is asked for goods, not activities.

sentence: What is the ___ of this jacket?
hint: the amount asked for goods in a shop
explanation: 'Price' is what a seller asks for goods; 'fee' is for professional services and 'charge' for the act of asking payment.

sentence: The bank makes no ___ for using its cash machines.
hint: money asked for a service; pattern: make a ___ for
explanation: 'Make a charge for something' means to ask payment for a service; 'tip' is extra money for good service.

sentence: Teenagers ___ hours every day on social media.
hint: to use time or money on something (neutral)
explanation: 'Spend time/money on something' is the neutral verb for using time or money; 'waste' implies useless use.

sentence: You ___ a lot of water by having such long showers.
hint: to use something valuable without needing to
explanation: 'Waste' means to use more than necessary; 'save' means the opposite — to avoid using.

sentence: We ___ money by cycling to work instead of driving.
hint: to keep money instead of spending it
explanation: 'Save money by doing something' means to avoid spending it; 'earn' means to receive money for work.

sentence: We had great ___ at the beach party.
explanation: 'Fun' is an uncountable noun meaning enjoyment; 'funny' is an adjective meaning causing laughter.

sentence: The comedian was so ___ that everyone cried with laughter.
explanation: 'Funny' is an adjective describing something that makes you laugh; 'fun' describes enjoyable experiences.

sentence: There is little ___ that the plan will be approved.
hint: pattern: little ___ that something will happen
explanation: 'Possibility that ...' is the standard pattern; 'opportunity' means a situation that lets you do something.

sentence: Studying abroad is a wonderful ___ to practise your Spanish.
hint: a situation that lets you do something; pattern: ___ to do
explanation: 'Opportunity to do something' means a chance a situation gives you; 'possibility' is not followed by 'to'.

sentence: Our team has a good ___ of winning on Saturday.
hint: pattern: have a good ___ of doing something
explanation: 'Have a chance of doing something' is the standard collocation for the likelihood of success.

sentence: She wore ___ heels to the party.
explanation: 'High heels' is the fixed collocation; 'tall' is used for people, buildings and trees.

sentence: My brother is six foot three — he is much ___ than me.
explanation: 'Tall' is used for people's height, so the comparative is 'taller'; 'higher' is for heights above a level.

sentence: She studied ___ for her final exams.
hint: adverb meaning with a lot of effort
explanation: 'Hard' is an adverb meaning with great effort ('work hard'); 'hardly' means almost not at all.

sentence: There was ___ anything left in the fridge.
hint: adverb meaning almost not at all
explanation: 'Hardly' means almost not ('hardly anything'); 'hard' means with effort or solid.

sentence: The train arrived twenty minutes ___.
explanation: 'Late' means behind schedule; 'lately' means recently.

sentence: Have you seen him ___?
explanation: 'Lately' means recently and is typical with the present perfect; 'late' means behind time.

sentence: The hospital is ___ the city centre.
explanation: 'Near' is a preposition before a place; 'nearly' is an adverb of degree meaning almost; 'close' needs 'to'.

sentence: It was ___ midnight when we finally arrived.
explanation: 'Nearly' means almost; 'near' as a preposition needs a place object and cannot modify 'midnight'.

sentence: I love Italian food, ___ pizza.
explanation: 'Especially' means in particular or above all; 'specially' means for one particular purpose.

sentence: These shoes were ___ made for the customer.
explanation: 'Specially' means for a particular purpose ('specially made'); 'especially' means in particular.

sentence: ___ of the film, the hero rides off into the sunset.
hint: the final part of something (film, book, street)
explanation: 'At the end of something' refers to the final part; 'in the end' means finally, after a process.

sentence: We looked for the hotel for hours, but ___ we took a taxi.
explanation: 'In the end' means finally, after effort or difficulty; 'at the end' must be followed by 'of something'.

sentence: She sat ___ me during the whole flight.
explanation: 'Beside' means next to; 'besides' means in addition to.

sentence: ___ English, she speaks fluent Arabic.
explanation: 'Besides' means in addition to; 'beside' means next to; 'except' means not including.

sentence: The money was divided ___ the four children.
hint: for a group of more than two
explanation: 'Among' is traditionally used for more than two; 'between' is preferred for exactly two.

sentence: It's hard to choose ___ the two options.
explanation: 'Between' is used for two people or things; 'among' for a group of more than two.

sentence: We stayed in Rome ___ two weeks.
explanation: 'For' is used with a length of time; 'since' is used with a starting point; 'during' is followed by an event or period noun without a length.

sentence: She has lived in this street ___ 2015.
hint: starting point of a period up to now
explanation: 'Since' is used with a point in time when the situation started and continues; 'for' is used with a length of time.

sentence: Many people fell asleep ___ the lecture.
hint: within the period of an event
explanation: 'During' is followed by a noun (the lecture) and means within that time; 'while' needs a clause with a verb.

sentence: The stolen painting was extremely ___.
explanation: 'Valuable' means worth a lot of money; 'valued' means appreciated; 'invaluable' already means priceless, so it is not graded.

sentence: After twenty years of service, she is one of our most ___ employees.
explanation: 'A valued member/employee' is someone the organisation appreciates; 'valuable' stresses monetary or practical worth.

sentence: The new tax law will ___ every small business in the region.
explanation: 'Affect' is the verb (to influence); 'effect' is normally the noun.

sentence: The medicine had an immediate ___ on her breathing.
explanation: 'An effect on' — the noun form is required here.

sentence: Be careful not to ___ your passport at the check-in desk.
explanation: 'Lose' is the verb; 'loose' means not tight.

sentence: One of the screws on the bracket has come ___.
explanation: 'Come loose' = become not tight.

sentence: The committee will ___ your application at its May meeting.
explanation: The finite verb slot needs 'consider'; 'considerable' means large.

sentence: He gave a ___ summary of the 40-page report.
explanation: 'A brief summary' — adjective; 'briefly' is the adverb.

sentence: The two brothers are ___ in appearance but not in character.
explanation: 'They are alike' — 'alike' follows the verb and cannot come before a noun.

sentence: It's ___ to rain later, so take a coat.
explanation: 'It's likely to rain' — probable; 'alike' means similar.

sentence: The consultant will ___ us on every stage of the merger.
explanation: 'Advise' is the verb; 'advice' is the noun.

sentence: Take my ___ and sell the car before the prices fall.
explanation: 'Take my advice' — the noun form follows the possessive.

sentence: All ___ must wear identity badges at all times on site.
explanation: 'Personnel' = the employees of an organisation; 'personal' is an adjective.

sentence: She refused on ___ ; she would not bend the rules for anyone.
explanation: 'On principle' = because of one's moral rules.

sentence: The wine is the perfect ___ to the meal.
explanation: 'Complement' = something that completes or goes well with; 'compliment' is praise.

sentence: He ___ her on her presentation and her handling of questions.
explanation: 'Compliment someone on something' = praise them.
